concept.title: PARQUET_BLOOM_FILTER_WRITE Query Option ( or higher only)

conbody.p: PARQUET_BLOOM_FILTER_WRITE query option The PARQUET_BLOOM_FILTER_WRITE query option controls when Impala writes Parquet Bloom filters into the Parquet data files that it creates. Impala writes Bloom filters only for the columns that the table properties request them for, for example with the parquet.bloom.filter.columns table property. This query option cannot turn on Bloom filters for other columns. See for details.

The supported values for the query option are:
NEVER (0): Impala does not write Parquet Bloom filters, regardless of the table properties.
IF_NO_DICT (1): Impala writes the Bloom filter of a requested column only into the row groups where the column is not fully dictionary encoded. That happens when the column has too many distinct values for a dictionary, and Impala falls back from dictionary encoding to plain encoding. A fully dictionary encoded column chunk does not need a Bloom filter, because Impala can use the dictionary itself to skip row groups, see .
ALWAYS (2): Impala writes the Bloom filters of the requested columns into every row group, even where the column is fully dictionary encoded.
With the default IF_NO_DICT setting, the data files of a column with few distinct values usually contain no Bloom filter, even if the table properties request one.
When Impala reads Parquet files, it does not use the Bloom filter of a column chunk that is fully dictionary encoded. The ALWAYS setting is mainly useful when other engines read the data files.

Impala writes Parquet Bloom filters only for columns of the following types: TINYINT, SMALLINT, INT, BIGINT, FLOAT, DOUBLE, and STRING. Impala skips the requested columns of other types without raising an error.

For Iceberg tables, Impala also honors the Parquet Bloom filter table properties of Iceberg, such as write.parquet.bloom-filter-enabled.column.col. This query option controls writing the Bloom filters that those properties request, too. See for details.
